questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy, honestly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Little to none. We had an international student orientation which wasn't very good. That was all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It's kinda hard finding something good in LA. I did manage to get something via Zuma Housing - it's for students in LA and a lot of international students, too. It was a good place, but the landlord and company was a bit of a struggle at times.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Never say yes to a place before seeing it yourself or renting through a trusted and certified company. It's LA - there's a lot of bullshit going on. I was happy with my decision living off campus though - it made it easier for me to be there 100 when I was on campus as it gave me energy retracting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it was okay. a bit confusing but I figured it out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not really sure.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: get up in the middle of the night when registration starts a couple months before you arrive. it's nice to know what you'll do when you get there, and it's a horrible stress factor having to enroll when you have arrived - it will be hard getting good classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: it was really good and more film oriented than in Copenhagen which I loved.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Cant compare. they're total opposites 99% of the time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: two quarters: History of american film, Directing for film and television and Introductory screenwriting.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: all of them, but try some that is more niche - universities in the US has a lot of fun classes.

questions.answer: try the parties, movie clubs, sports clubs etc. stay on all kinds of different parts of campus after classes and go to art exhibitions by the students

questions.answer: as much as possible. all areas of LA, go up north, San Diego, OC the desert.

questions.answer: it was fun

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just do it

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: there's a big age gap between danish university students and americans

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: americans have an openness and "reach for the stars" mentality I love

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: prepare for high expenses on food and transportation, go to the international orientation, and enjoy the best place on earth

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: really budgeting

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: my classes, living in LA, my new friends from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the best and worst thing at the same time was being away from everything and everyone I know.
